verses.english: “Mendicants, there are these four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
These are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

verses.pali: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṁ satipaṭṭhānānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—
verses.english: Because of developing and cultivating these four kinds of mindfulness meditation, one of two results can be expected:

verses.pali: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā”ti.
verses.english: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”
